properties.name: BL-198 step 1 landed by REMOVING `default:` from ten properties, not by changing code. The route changed on a measurement: `default:` in the schema YAML is not documentation — dynograph-core applies it at WRITE time (schema.rs:507 inserts any missing property that declares one), which is where 3,207 stored values across 59% of the design came from. So export-side suppression could never have worked — the store cannot tell a chosen value from an injected one — and the real fix is one YAML token per property. FORWARD-ONLY: nodes already written keep what they hold, so the export does not churn and compare_designs sees nothing; the phantom-diff cost this epoch was scoped around does not arise on this route at all. TEN of 81 removed, 71 kept, and the RATIO is the finding: three mechanically-obvious candidates turned out to be meaningful and were kept on evidence.
